definitions.explanation: The state of having nothing in one's hands — no weapons, tools, or resources. Used both literally to mean fighting with bare fists and figuratively to mean starting with nothing.

examples.japanese: {空拳|くうけん}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{戦|たたか}う→戦う：02071_tatakau⟧。
⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{空拳|くうけん}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{事業|じぎょう}→事業：11421_jigyou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{立|た}ち{上|あ}げた→立ち上げる：07892_tachiageru⟧。
examples.english: He built the business from nothing.

examples.japanese: ⟦{武器|ぶき}→武器：03605_buki⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{道具|どうぐ}→道具：01479_dougu⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦なく→ない：01118_nai⟧{空拳|くうけん}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{困難|こんなん}→困難：01410_konnan⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{立|た}ち{向|む}かわなければ→立ち向かう：06981_tachimukau⟧⟦ならなかった→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: Without weapons or tools, we had to face the difficulty empty-handed.

notes:
Literally "empty fists," composed of ⟦{空|くう}→空〜：03949_kuu⟧ (empty) and {拳|けん} (fist). Used both in martial arts contexts to mean fighting without weapons and figuratively to describe starting an endeavor with no resources or capital.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {空拳|くうけん}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{戦|たたか}う→戦う：02071_tatakau⟧: fight bare-handed
- {空拳|くうけん}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{始|はじ}める: start from nothing
- {徒手|としゅ}{空拳|くうけん}: completely empty-handed (four-character compound emphasizing total lack of resources)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{素手|すで}→素手：13817_sude⟧: bare hands (more common in everyday speech)
- ⟦{徒手|としゅ}→徒手：26454_toshu⟧: empty-handed (often paired with {空拳|くうけん})
- ⟦{丸腰|まるごし}→丸腰：27230_marugoshi⟧: unarmed (specifically without weapons)

USAGE:
The four-character compound {徒手|としゅ}{空拳|くうけん} is a well-known expression meaning to have absolutely no resources, capital, or advantages. It is frequently used when describing entrepreneurs who built something from nothing.
